title: HB778 (2024 Regular): Assault weapons; prohibit sale of to any person under age 21 years.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Mississippi) (gun-policy Stage 5, Mississippi); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Mississippi text (Introduced; official copy, https://billstatus.ls.state.ms.us/documents/2024/html/HB/0700-0799/HB0778IN.htm)
provenance.note: As-filed text, no date; no passage vote recorded. Section 2 prints two versions of 97-37-1 (conditional on Chapter 461, Laws 2023); Section 5 only brings forward 45-9-101 (concealed carry licences) unchanged. Section 1 (2) ends 'unless the person is a member of any branch of the United States Armed Forces'. List items (a)-(j) of the definition omitted from the quote.

operative_text:
Section 1 (new section): (1) For purposes of this act, the term "assault weapon" means a selective-fire firearm capable of fully automatic, semiautomatic, or burst fire at the user's option; any of more than One Hundred Fifty (150) named semiautomatic firearms, including semiautomatic centerfire rifles and semiautomatic pistols; a semiautomatic firearm that has certain features; and a shotgun with a revolving cylinder, including any part or combination of parts designed or intended to convert a firearm into an assault weapon or any combination of parts from which one may be rapidly assembled if possessed or controlled by the same person. (2) It shall be unlawful for any person to give, distribute, transport, or import an assault weapon; or keep, offer, or expose any such weapon for sale to any person less than twenty-one (21) years of age, unless the person is a member of any branch of the United States Armed Forces.
Section 2 (Miss. Code § 97-37-1): (2) Except as otherwise provided in Section 1 of this act, it shall not be a violation of this section for any person over the age of eighteen (18) years to carry a firearm or deadly weapon concealed within the confines of his own home or his place of business, or any real property associated with his home or business or within any motor vehicle.
Section 3 (Miss. Code § 45-9-53): (1) Except as otherwise provided in Section 1 of this act, this section and Section 45-9-51 do not affect the authority that a county or municipality may have under another law:
Section 4 (Miss. Code § 45-9-57): Except as otherwise provided in Section 1 of this act, a county may regulate the discharge of any firearm or weapon, other than a BB gun, within any platted subdivision.
